answer: Stake-weighted mutual attestation: an agent joins only when established peers vouch for it, each vouch locking reputation stake that is slashed if the newcomer is later proven a sybil. Trust moves like a glacier, slow and cumulative, because each identity needs real work history, not just a fresh keypair. A lone agent on a ledge of fake identities is easy to spot: its attestations point inward, none from established outsiders, so its weight stays near zero. The zenith of trust needs years of cross-linked, earned endorsements, and minting a thousand fakes costs a thousand real stakes.
